summary: This Wikipedia-derived note is an overview of New Zealand, an island country in the southwest Pacific covering its geography, Etymology, history from Polynesian settlement through British colonisation to independence, government and politics, foreign relations and military. It describes a constitutional monarchy with an MMP electoral system, a developed economy shaped by 1980s liberalisation, and a population mainly of European descent with Māori as the largest minority. The excerpt ends partway through the foreign relations and military section.
one_line: Overview of New Zealand's geography, Māori and colonial history, constitutional monarchy, politics, and foreign relations in the southwest Pacific.
key_facts: New Zealand is an island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean consisting of the North Island (Te Ika-a-Māui) and the South Island (Te Waipounamu) plus over 700 smaller islands.
New Zealand's capital city is Wellington and its most populous city is Auckland.
Abel Tasman became the first European to sight and record New Zealand in 1642.
James Cook became the first European to set foot on and map New Zealand in 1769.
The Treaty of Waitangi was first signed in the Bay of Islands on 6 February 1840.
New Zealand became a dominion in 1907 and gained full statutory independence in 1947 through the Statute of Westminster Adoption Act.
In 1893 New Zealand was the first nation in the world to grant all women the right to vote.
The Liberals guaranteed a minimum wage in 1894, described in the note as a world first.
New Zealand's Parliament holds legislative power and consists of the king and the House of Representatives; the Legislative Council was abolished in 1950.
Since the 1996 election, New Zealand has used mixed-member proportional (MMP) voting, with 72 electorates and 48 list seats out of 120.
Christopher Luxon has been the 42nd prime minister since 27 November 2023.
The 2018 census recorded a population of 4,699,755, with 70.2% European and 16.5% Māori ethnicity.
Māori made up 45% of New Zealanders convicted of crimes and 53% of those imprisoned, while being 16.5% of the population.
In 1886 New Zealand annexed the Kermadec Islands, about 1,000 km northeast of Auckland.
Since 1951 New Zealand joined Australia and the United States in the ANZUS security treaty.
